The PSI of Ashoknagar Police Station submitted charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
. The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-

The case of the prosecution is that the complainant had contracted the work to the accused person to renovation of his apartment No.F2, Wellington Court, 45,
Wellington Street, Richmond Town, Bengaluru - 560025 for the estimated amount of Rs.5,10,300/- within the period of 45 days and they both agreed and entered into an agreement on 16.02.2018.
The complainant made all the payments in accordance with the agreement to the accused person.
The complainant made total payment of Rs.5,10,300/- and received payments confirmation receipts from him.
Thereafter, the accused person was worked highly irregularity and he was not being completed as per the timelines of the agreement.

When the complainant requested the accused person and demanded to complete the work on several times but the accused person stopped responding his calls, messages and emails, The complainant decided to terminate the contract of the accused and requested to refund the amount for which work was not completed.

But the accused person neither complete the renovation work of apartment of the building and nor return the non completion of C.C.No.20698/2019 renovation work of the building an amount of Rs.4,02,580/- and thereby the accused person has committed the criminal breach of trust and cheated the complainant and committed the above offences.
After completion of the investigation the PSI of Ashoknagar Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.

During the course of cross examination by the learned Sr. APP nothing has been elicited from his mouth.
14. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations against the accused person under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused person beyond all reasonable doubt.

In view of the same, this court hold Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
15. Point No.3: For the reasons stated and finding given to point Nos.1 and 2, the following is made.
ORDER
The accused person is not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
Acting under section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure the accused person is C.C.No.20698/2019 hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond executed by him stand canceled.
